english:
Rock fishing begins before dawn, in pitch darkness under a sky of falling stars. You load your heavy gear onto the ferry boat and set off straight for the open sea.
Some days the sea is glassy calm; on rough days, choppy peaks of waves rise all around.
The ferry races at full speed toward the reef you're headed for. Now and then a big swell slams the hull, and each jolt runs through your whole body.
As the starlight blurs and fades away, the eastern sky begins to pale. Light in every color of the rainbow sets the clouds aglow before sunrise.
Before long, a fierce light bursts from a single point on the horizon. In an instant, the stillness is broken from that one spot. The sun quickly shows its face, and by the time it stands clear of the horizon, the eastern sky is bright with day. But under the sea, where the light has yet to reach, it is still pitch dark.
Now and then, flying fish startled by the boat spread their clear fins and sail hundreds of meters through the morning sun, sparkling as they go.
At last the ferry reaches the fishing grounds. Big swells surge up the reef and slide back down. The boat noses its bow against a rock where the swell is gentler, and one by one the anglers leap off, timing their jump to the rise and fall of the boat. Without a pause, the heavy gear is tossed across, piece after piece. It's all over in the blink of an eye.

{FFFC}
Those after bottom fish drive pitons into the rock and set their rods in place. Those after fish near the surface cast their rigs out toward the horizon. Toss some chum into the water, and you can see the fish gather. Some get so excited they swim about belly-up.
The set rod twitches up and down. You watch it for a moment, then lean back hard all at once to set the hook. The startled fish thrashes wildly, trying to throw the hook. It nearly drags the rod away with it. You open the reel and let out line. After a while, the fish starts to slow.
Again and again you raise the rod, haul the fish closer with all your strength, and reel in. You can't relax for even a moment, or the fish will pull your rod down flat in an instant. Snapped leaders, broken hooks and thrown hooks happen all the time.
The hooked fish thrashes left and right. Each time, you shift your footing so it can't dive into the rocks below. It's one tense moment after another. Then, after a battle of many long minutes, the fish finally gives out.

{FFFD}
This is truly the happiest moment there is. For this one moment, it lets you forget everything else. Joy simply wells up inside you. With a really big one, you might even shed a tear.
And so, again and again, you head out, still chasing the bite of a giant fish you've never yet seen.

english:
At last, it's time to head home. The ferry has come to pick everyone up near the fishing spots.
Those who caught plenty and those who caught little all wear the same refreshed look. It's the look of people who have enjoyed the great outdoors to the fullest.
Those who landed a big one will want to come again, and those who didn't will want to come back and try once more.
With waters so full of fish that an angler never tires, and all of nature's bounty to savor, rock fishing truly is the finest pastime there is.

{center}Farewell
